question: Which type of foundation is most suitable for a multi-storey building constructed on soft, compressible soil where load-bearing strata are located at considerable depth?
options: Strip foundation
Pad foundation
Pile foundation
Raft foundation

question: In reinforced concrete design, the term 'cover' refers to which of the following?
options: The thickness of the formwork used during casting
The distance between the outer face of the concrete and the nearest surface of the reinforcement
The overlap length of steel bars at splices
The depth of the neutral axis from the compression face

question: A builder notices that efflorescence has appeared on the face of a newly completed brick wall. What is the primary cause of this defect?
options: Inadequate mortar mix proportions causing shrinkage cracks
Soluble salts within the masonry materials being carried to the surface by moisture movement
Thermal expansion of the bricks due to direct sunlight exposure
Incorrect brick bond causing stress concentrations at the wall face

question: When designing a timber roof truss, the member that resists the horizontal outward thrust at the eaves and prevents the rafters from spreading is called the?
options: Ridge board
Purlin
Collar tie
Tie beam

question: Which of the following correctly describes the purpose of a damp proof course (DPC) in a cavity wall construction?
options: To improve the thermal insulation properties of the wall
To prevent the upward migration of ground moisture into the wall structure
To provide structural continuity between the inner and outer leaves
To act as a fire barrier within the cavity

question: In soil mechanics, a Standard Penetration Test (SPT) is used primarily to determine which property of soil?
options: Liquid limit and plasticity index
In-situ density and shear strength characteristics
Particle size distribution and grading
Permeability coefficient and drainage rate

question: Which type of bond is most commonly used for a 215 mm (one-brick) thick wall requiring maximum strength and structural integrity?
options: Stretcher bond
English bond
Flemish bond
Header bond

question: A quantity surveyor preparing a Bill of Quantities uses the 'Standard Method of Measurement' (SMM). What is the primary purpose of this document?
options: To specify the quality of materials to be used on site
To provide a uniform basis for measuring and describing building work
To determine the construction programme and sequence of operations
To calculate the structural loads imposed on the foundation

question: In plumbing systems, a trap is installed beneath sanitary fittings. What is the critical dimension used to evaluate the effectiveness of a trap?
options: The diameter of the trap outlet
The water seal depth, which must be a minimum of 50 mm
The length of the inlet arm connecting the fitting to the trap
The gradient of the waste pipe downstream of the trap

question: Which of the following best describes the structural behaviour of a simply supported beam under a uniformly distributed load?
options: Maximum bending moment occurs at the supports, and shear force is zero at mid-span
Maximum bending moment occurs at mid-span, and shear force is zero at mid-span
Maximum bending moment occurs at mid-span, and maximum shear force occurs at the supports
Maximum bending moment and maximum shear force both occur at the supports

question: In electrical installations, the term 'ring final circuit' is used. Which statement most accurately describes this circuit configuration?
options: A single cable run from the consumer unit to each socket outlet in series, terminating at the last outlet
Both ends of the circuit cable are connected to the same way in the consumer unit, forming a continuous loop
The circuit uses a radial layout with all sockets protected by a 32A circuit breaker
Each socket outlet is individually protected by its own fuse in the consumer unit

question: During concrete production, the water-cement ratio has a direct effect on concrete quality. An increase in the water-cement ratio will result in which of the following?
options: Increased compressive strength and reduced workability
Reduced compressive strength and increased workability
Increased compressive strength and increased workability
Reduced compressive strength and reduced workability

question: A building contract includes a 'Retention Fund' clause. What is the primary purpose of the retention fund?
options: To finance the purchase of materials at the start of the project
To provide a financial incentive for the contractor to complete snagging items and meet defects liability obligations
To cover the cost of variations ordered by the architect during construction
To compensate the client for any liquidated and ascertained damages imposed on the contractor

question: Which roof covering system relies on the principle of capillary action being broken by an upstand or anti-capillary groove to prevent water ingress at lapped joints?
options: Clay pantiles
Corrugated fibre cement sheets
Single-ply membrane roofing
Built-up felt roofing

question: In the context of construction project management, the Critical Path Method (CPM) is used. Which statement best defines the critical path?
options: The sequence of activities that requires the greatest financial expenditure during the project
The longest sequence of dependent activities through the network that determines the minimum project duration
The path that identifies all activities with the highest risk of delay or failure
The shortest route through the project network connecting the start and finish milestones
